titulo: All About My Home and What I Love
titulo_es: Todo sobre mi casa y lo que me gusta
estandares: Describo con oraciones simples mi casa, mi entorno y los objetos que me rodean. Identifico la cantidad y la ubicación de las cosas en textos y descripciones cortas.
competencias: Describir lugares y objetos usando preposiciones de lugar, plurales y expresiones de cantidad; preguntar y responder sobre lo que hay en un espacio; escribir descripciones cortas de la casa y de las cosas favoritas.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante diseña el plano de una casa y la describe por escrito y en voz alta: qué habitaciones tiene, qué muebles hay en cada una y dónde está cada objeto.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student designs the plan of a house and describes it in writing and out loud: which rooms it has, what furniture is in each one and where every object is.

lecciones.content_es:
¿Dónde está?

Las preposiciones de lugar dicen la posición exacta de una cosa.

  • in – dentro de: The keys are in the drawer.
  • on – sobre una superficie: The lamp is on the table.
  • under – debajo · behind – detrás · in front of – delante
  • next to – al lado · between – entre dos · near – cerca

Cómo se usan

Siempre van antes del lugar: The cat is under the bed.

Diferencia clave: in es adentro de un espacio cerrado, on es apoyado encima de algo.
lecciones.content_en:
Where is it?

Prepositions of place tell the exact position of something.

  • in – inside: The keys are in the drawer.
  • on – on a surface: The lamp is on the table.
  • under · behind · in front of
  • next to · between (two things) · near

How to use them

They always come before the place: The cat is under the bed.

Key difference: in means inside a closed space, on means resting on a surface.

fichas.d_en: Inside a closed space: in the box.

fichas.d: Sobre una superficie: on the table.
fichas.d_en: On a surface: on the table.

fichas.d_en: Between two things: between the sofa and the door.

fichas.d: Al lado de: next to the window.
fichas.d_en: Beside: next to the window.

fichas.d: Delante de / detrás de.
fichas.d_en: In front of / behind.

quiz.why_en: On means something rests on a surface.

quiz.q_en: "My house is ___ the school and the park."

quiz.why_en: Between is used when something is in the middle of two places.

quiz.why: Behind indica que algo está en la parte de atrás.
quiz.why_en: Behind means something is at the back.

lecciones.content_es:
La regla general

Se agrega -s: book → books, chair → chairs.

Casos especiales

  • -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -o → -es: box → boxes, watch → watches
  • consonante + y → -ies: city → cities
  • -f / -fe → -ves: knife → knives, shelf → shelves

Irregulares

man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, person → people. Y algunos no cambian: fish → fish, sheep → sheep.
lecciones.content_en:
The general rule

Add -s: book → books, chair → chairs.

Special cases

  • -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -x, -o → -es: box → boxes, watch → watches
  • consonant + y → -ies: city → cities
  • -f / -fe → -ves: knife → knives, shelf → shelves

Irregular ones

man → men, woman → women, child → children, foot → feet, tooth → teeth, person → people. Some do not change: fish → fish, sheep → sheep.

lecciones.t: Cantidad: there is / there are en negativo y pregunta
lecciones.t_en: Quantity: there is / there are in negatives and questions
lecciones.content_es:
Decir cuánto hay

  • Afirmativo: There is a sofa. / There are three chairs.
  • Negativo: There isn't a TV. / There aren't any lamps.
  • Pregunta: Is there a garden? / Are there any pictures?

Respuestas cortas

Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. — Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

How many…?

Para preguntar la cantidad exacta: How many rooms are there in your house? → There are five.
lecciones.content_en:
Saying how much there is

  • Affirmative: There is a sofa. / There are three chairs.
  • Negative: There isn't a TV. / There aren't any lamps.
  • Question: Is there a garden? / Are there any pictures?

Short answers

Yes, there is. / No, there isn't. — Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.

How many…?

To ask for the exact number: How many rooms are there in your house? → There are five.

fichas.d: Negación en singular: no hay un/una.
fichas.d_en: Singular negative form.

fichas.d: Negación en plural, casi siempre con any.
fichas.d_en: Plural negative, almost always with any.

fichas.d: Pregunta por la cantidad exacta de cosas contables.
fichas.d_en: Asks for the exact number of countable things.

fichas.d: Respuesta corta afirmativa en plural.
fichas.d_en: Affirmative short answer in the plural.

quiz.why: Chairs es plural, así que la pregunta empieza con Are there.
quiz.why_en: Chairs is plural, so the question starts with Are there.

quiz.q: Respuesta corta a «Is there a garage?» (no hay)
quiz.q_en: Short answer to "Is there a garage?" (there isn't one)
quiz.why: La respuesta corta repite there + is en negativo.
quiz.why_en: The short answer repeats there + is in the negative.

quiz.why: Bedrooms es contable, así que se pregunta con How many.
quiz.why_en: Bedrooms is countable, so we ask with How many.

lecciones.content_es:
La regla básica

  • some en oraciones afirmativas: There are some books on the desk.
  • any en negativas y preguntas: There aren't any books. / Are there any books?

La excepción amable

Cuando ofrecemos o pedimos algo se usa some aunque sea pregunta: Would you like some juice?

Con qué van

Se usan con sustantivos plurales (some chairs) y con incontables (some water, some bread).
lecciones.content_en:
The basic rule

  • some in affirmative sentences: There are some books on the desk.
  • any in negatives and questions: There aren't any books. / Are there any books?

The polite exception

When we offer or request something we use some even in questions: Would you like some juice?

What they go with

They are used with plural nouns (some chairs) and with uncountable nouns (some water, some bread).

fichas.d: Algunos/algo, en oraciones afirmativas.
fichas.d_en: Used in affirmative sentences.

fichas.d: En negaciones y preguntas: any books?
fichas.d_en: Used in negatives and questions: any books?

fichas.d: Excepción: ofrecimientos llevan some aunque sean preguntas.
fichas.d_en: Exception: offers take some even in questions.

fichas.d: Con incontables no se usa número: some water, some bread.
fichas.d_en: With uncountable nouns there is no number: some water, some bread.

quiz.why: En oraciones negativas se usa any.
quiz.why_en: In negative sentences we use any.

quiz.why: Es una oración afirmativa con plural: some.
quiz.why_en: It is an affirmative sentence with a plural noun: some.

quiz.why: Es un ofrecimiento, y los ofrecimientos usan some.
quiz.why_en: It is an offer, and offers take some.

lecciones.content_es:
Suenan igual, significan distinto

  • they're = they are (ellos son/están): They're my cousins.
  • their = posesivo (su, de ellos): Their house is big.
  • there = allí, o el «hay» de there is/are: The park is over there.

Cómo no equivocarse

Prueba a reemplazar por they are: si la oración sigue teniendo sentido, va they're. Si después viene un sustantivo del que se dice el dueño, va their. Si hablas de un lugar o de existencia, va there.
lecciones.content_en:
They sound the same, they mean different things

  • they're = they are: They're my cousins.
  • their = possessive: Their house is big.
  • there = a place, or the there of there is/are: The park is over there.

How to get it right

Try replacing it with they are: if the sentence still makes sense, use they're. If a noun with an owner follows, use their. If you are talking about a place or existence, use there.

fichas.d: Contracción de they are.
fichas.d_en: Contraction of they are.

fichas.d: Adjetivo posesivo: de ellos.
fichas.d_en: Possessive adjective: belonging to them.

fichas.d: Allí, o el sujeto de there is / there are.
fichas.d_en: There as a place, or in there is / there are.

fichas.d: Si puedes decir they are, entonces se escribe they're.
fichas.d_en: If you can say they are, then it is written they're.

quiz.why: Acompaña al sustantivo bikes y dice de quién son: their.
quiz.why_en: It goes with the noun bikes and says who owns them: their.

quiz.q_en: "___ is a big tree in my garden."

quiz.why_en: It is the there is structure used to say something exists.

quiz.why_en: It is equivalent to they are my best friends.

lecciones.t: Presente simple: reglas de escritura del verbo
lecciones.content_es:
Repaso rápido

Afirmativo con -s en he/she/it; negativo e interrogativo con do/does y el verbo en forma base.

Las reglas de escritura

  • Regla general: work → works, read → reads
  • -o, -ch, -sh, -ss, -x → -es: do → does, teach → teaches, fix → fixes
  • consonante + y → -ies: cry → cries, fly → flies
  • vocal + y → solo -s: play → plays, buy → buys
  • irregular: have → has

Trampa frecuente

play lleva vocal antes de la y, por eso es plays y no plaies.
lecciones.content_en:
Quick review

Affirmative with -s for he/she/it; negative and question with do/does and the base verb.

Spelling rules

  • General rule: work → works, read → reads
  • -o, -ch, -sh, -ss, -x → -es: do → does, teach → teaches, fix → fixes
  • consonant + y → -ies: cry → cries, fly → flies
  • vowel + y → just -s: play → plays, buy → buys
  • irregular: have → has

Common trap

play has a vowel before the y, so it is plays and not plaies.

fichas.d: Verbos en -ch agregan -es.
fichas.d_en: Verbs ending in -ch add -es.

fichas.d: Consonante + y se convierte en -ies.
fichas.d_en: Consonant + y becomes -ies.

fichas.d: Vocal + y solo agrega -s.
fichas.d_en: Vowel + y just adds -s.

fichas.d: Se escribe con -es y además funciona como auxiliar.
fichas.d_en: It takes -es and also works as the auxiliary.

quiz.why: Do termina en -o, así que en tercera persona es does.
quiz.why_en: Do ends in -o, so the third person is does.

quiz.why: Play tiene vocal antes de la y: solo se agrega -s.
quiz.why_en: Play has a vowel before the y: it only adds -s.

quiz.why: Regla general de tercera persona: se agrega -s.
quiz.why_en: General third person rule: add -s.

lecciones.content_es:
Decir de quién es algo

Se pone 's al dueño y luego el objeto: Ana's room = el cuarto de Ana.

Reglas

  • Dueño singular → 's: my brother's bike
  • Plural terminado en -s → solo ': my parents' car
  • Plural irregular → 's: the children's toys
  • Varios dueños del mismo objeto → 's solo al último: Ana and Luis's house

Ojo

El genitivo se usa sobre todo con personas y animales. Con objetos se prefiere of: the door of the house.
lecciones.content_en:
Saying who owns something

Add 's to the owner and then the object: Ana's room = the room of Ana.

Rules

  • Singular owner → 's: my brother's bike
  • Plural ending in -s → just ': my parents' car
  • Irregular plural → 's: the children's toys
  • Two owners of the same thing → 's only on the last one: Ana and Luis's house

Careful

The possessive is used mostly with people and animals. With objects we prefer of: the door of the house.

fichas.d: 's indica el dueño: el cuarto de Ana.
fichas.d_en: 's marks the owner: the room of Ana.

fichas.d: Plural en -s: solo apóstrofe, sin s extra.
fichas.d_en: Plural ending in -s: apostrophe only, no extra s.

fichas.d: Plural irregular: sí lleva 's.
fichas.d_en: Irregular plural: it does take 's.

fichas.d: Con objetos se prefiere of en lugar del genitivo.
fichas.d_en: With objects we prefer of instead of the possessive.

quiz.q: ¿Cómo se dice «el carro de mis padres»?
quiz.q_en: How do you say "my parents' car"?
quiz.why: Parents ya termina en -s, así que solo lleva apóstrofe.
quiz.why_en: Parents already ends in -s, so it takes only an apostrophe.

quiz.why: Dueño singular: se agrega 's.
quiz.why_en: Singular owner: add 's.

quiz.why: Children es plural irregular, así que lleva 's completo.
quiz.why_en: Children is an irregular plural, so it takes the full 's.

lecciones.content_es:
Cardinales

one, two, three… thirteen (13), twenty (20), thirty (30), fifty (50), one hundred (100), one thousand (1000).

De 21 en adelante se une con guion: twenty-one, forty-five.

Ordinales

Dicen el orden: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), y del cuarto en adelante se agrega -th: fourth, fifth, twentieth.

Dónde se usan

Fechas (May 3rd), pisos (the second floor), edad y cantidades (There are twelve chairs).
lecciones.content_en:
Cardinal numbers

one, two, three… thirteen (13), twenty (20), thirty (30), fifty (50), one hundred (100), one thousand (1000).

From 21 on they are joined with a hyphen: twenty-one, forty-five.

Ordinal numbers

They give order: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), and from fourth on you add -th: fourth, fifth, twentieth.

Where they are used

Dates (May 3rd), floors (the second floor), age and quantities (There are twelve chairs).

fichas.d: 13 y 30: el acento cambia y la escritura también.
fichas.d_en: 13 and 30: stress and spelling are different.

fichas.d: De 21 en adelante se escribe con guion.
fichas.d_en: From 21 on, numbers use a hyphen.

fichas.d: Los tres primeros ordinales son irregulares.
fichas.d_en: The first three ordinals are irregular.

fichas.d: Terminación de la mayoría de los ordinales: fourth, tenth.
fichas.d_en: Ending of most ordinals: fourth, tenth.

quiz.why: Se escribe forty (sin u) y con guion: forty-five.
quiz.why_en: It is spelled forty (no u) and hyphenated: forty-five.

quiz.why: Third es uno de los tres ordinales irregulares.
quiz.why_en: Third is one of the three irregular ordinals.

quiz.why: Los pisos se dicen con ordinal: second floor.
quiz.why_en: Floors use ordinals: second floor.

lecciones.content_es:
Habitaciones

living room – sala · dining room – comedor · kitchen – cocina · bedroom – dormitorio · bathroom – baño · garage – garaje · garden – jardín · stairs – escaleras.

Muebles

sofa, armchair (sillón), table, chair, bed, wardrobe (armario), desk (escritorio), shelf (repisa), mirror (espejo), lamp.

Descripción típica

In my bedroom there is a bed, a desk and a big wardrobe. The lamp is on the desk.

Rooms

living room · dining room · kitchen · bedroom · bathroom · garage · garden · stairs.

Furniture

sofa, armchair, table, chair, bed, wardrobe, desk, shelf, mirror, lamp.

A typical description

In my bedroom there is a bed, a desk and a big wardrobe. The lamp is on the desk.

lecciones.content_es:
Hablar de gustos

  • I like… / I love… / I don't like… / I hate…
  • My favorite color is blue.
  • What's your favorite food? — It's pizza.

Categorías útiles

colors: red, blue, green, yellow, black, white, purple, orange.
hobbies: reading, drawing, dancing, playing video games, listening to music.
things: my phone, my bike, my guitar, my dog.

Detalle importante

Después de like el verbo va en -ing: I like reading.
lecciones.content_en:
Talking about what you like

  • I like… / I love… / I don't like… / I hate…
  • My favorite color is blue.
  • What's your favorite food? — It's pizza.

Useful categories

colors: red, blue, green, yellow, black, white, purple, orange.
hobbies: reading, drawing, dancing, playing video games, listening to music.
things: my phone, my bike, my guitar, my dog.

Important detail

After like the verb takes -ing: I like reading.

repaso.titulo: Repaso — All About My Home and What I Love
repaso.titulo_en: Review — All About My Home and What I Love
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Este periodo se trata de describir espacios y cosas. Para eso combinas tres herramientas: las preposiciones de lugar (in, on, under, between…), el plural de los sustantivos y las expresiones de cantidad (there is/are, some/any, how many).

Puntos gramaticales

  • Plural: -s, -es, -ies, -ves, más los irregulares (children, people, feet).
  • some en afirmativo; any en negativo y pregunta; some en ofrecimientos.
  • they're (they are) / their (posesivo) / there (lugar o existencia).
  • Genitivo sajón: Ana's room, my parents' car, the children's toys.

Vocabulario

Números cardinales y ordinales, habitaciones, muebles, objetos de la casa y cosas favoritas.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

This term is about describing spaces and things. You combine three tools: prepositions of place (in, on, under, between…), noun plurals, and quantity expressions (there is/are, some/any, how many).

Grammar points

  • Plurals: -s, -es, -ies, -ves, plus irregulars (children, people, feet).
  • some in affirmatives; any in negatives and questions; some in offers.
  • they're (they are) / their (possessive) / there (place or existence).
  • Possessive 's: Ana's room, my parents' car, the children's toys.

Vocabulary

Cardinal and ordinal numbers, rooms, furniture, household objects and favorite things.
puntos_clave: in = adentro; on = sobre una superficie.
in = inside; on = on a surface.
some en afirmativo, any en negativo y pregunta.
some in affirmatives, any in negatives and questions.
Plural en -s ya escrito: solo apóstrofe (my parents').
Plural already ending in -s: apostrophe only (my parents').
they're = they are; their = posesivo; there = allí / hay.
they're = they are; their = possessive; there = place / existence.
Después de like el verbo va en -ing.
After like the verb takes the -ing form.
